Title: Trump administration likely to shed 300,000 workers in 2025: OPM director

Summary: 
The Trump administration is expected to shed around 300,000 workers by the end of 2025, according to Office of Personnel Management director Scott Kupor. This would represent a 12.5 percent reduction from the federal workforce at the time of President Trump's inauguration. Kupor stated, 'I cannot force people to lay people off,' and attributed the mass departures to voluntary buyouts rather than firings. As of May, nearly 60,000 federal employees had been cut or laid off, with an additional 150,000 planned reductions across various agencies. The Department of Government Efficiency, led by billionaire Elon Musk, has been driving the administration's efforts, but its momentum has slowed due to Musk's departure and court orders blocking parts of its agenda.

Title: Recortes al Departamento de Eficiencia de EU ascenderán a 300,000 puestos este año

Summary: 
According to a new report, the Trump administration will cut 300,000 federal employees by the end of September 2025, reducing the federal workforce from 2.4 million to 2.1 million. Scott Kupor, director of the Office of Personnel Management, told the New York Times that he does not expect new significant layoffs before year‑end and that most of the 300,000 employees have already left, though some remain on payroll: 'no espera nuevos anuncios significativos de despidos antes de fin de año.' He noted that 80 % of the employees were voluntary retirees and 20 % were dismissed. The 2023 attrition rate was 5.9 % (Partnership for Public Service). Major agencies affected include USAID, which was entirely dissolved with a 10,000‑person cut; the Department of Health and Human Services, which lost about 20,000 staff (≈ 24 % of its workforce); and the Food and Drug Administration, which eliminated roughly 3,500 employees (≈ 16.7 %). Trump appointed Elon Musk to lead the Department of Government Efficiency to identify agencies for cuts, a move that drew bipartisan criticism. Trump said the cuts were intended to eliminate waste and bureaucracy: 'los recortes estaban diseñados para eliminar el despilfarro y la burocracia gubernamental.' Critics argued they removed key expertise and threatened essential services. Many of the dismissed workers were in probationary positions, and several lawsuits were filed by employees, advocacy groups, unions, and local governments, though the Supreme Court ruled in July that most layoffs could proceed.

Title: Estados Unidos pagará a más de 150 000 funcionarios para que no regresen a sus puestos de trabajo - El Tiempo

Summary: 
The US government has agreed to pay over 154,000 public employees to leave their positions before December 31, 2025, as part of a strategy to gradually reduce the federal workforce without sudden layoffs that would affect public services. According to a spokesperson for the Office of Personnel Management, these employees will continue to receive their salaries during the process. However, this number represents only about 6% of the total number of federal employees in the US administration, which has approximately 2.3 million employees. President Trump has promoted an aggressive policy of reducing personnel since taking office, arguing that it will eliminate what he calls 'an inflated bureaucracy.' The Department of State has announced the dismissal of over 1,300 employees in the US and abroad, and several federal departments have initiated internal evaluations to review the number and function of their employees, with a view to future additional cuts. Democratic senators have presented a critical report questioning the economic cost of 'deferred resignation,' which they say has cost the government billions of dollars in salaries for employees who are no longer providing effective services. The report also criticizes the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE), led by Elon Musk, for wasting up to $21.7 billion on unclear actions and unproductive systems. The DOGE has been under Musk's direction since 2024, when Trump appointed him as part of his economic cabinet. Critics argue that the lack of oversight over the DOGE's spending has generated more questions than benefits, while the White House's proposed savings goals have not yet materialized effectively.

Published date: August 01 2025, 16:34

Title: EUA oficializam demissão voluntária de 154 mil funcionários

Summary: 
The U.S. government, under President Donald Trump (Republican Party), officially announced the voluntary dismissal of 154,000 federal employees on Tuesday, September 30, 2025, marking the largest single-year reduction in federal workforce in 80 years. The move, implemented with assistance from Elon Musk, who was part of the Doge (Department of Government Efficiency), is part of a broader initiative to shrink the federal bureaucracy. The program offered financial incentives and advance notice to employees who did not accept voluntary departure packages, with many remaining on payroll even after ceasing duties. Dismissals began on Wednesday, October 1, 2025, affecting key agencies including NASA (approximately 4,000 employees), the National Weather Service (around 200), the CDC (Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, about 2,400), and the FDA (Food and Drug Administration, roughly 3,500). The Agricultural Research Service of the Department of Agriculture saw about 1,200 employees—17% of its workforce—accept the packages. Trump argues that the federal workforce has become too large and inefficient. The administration aims to dismiss approximately 300,000 workers by the end of 2025, representing a 12.5% reduction in the federal workforce since January. The federal government spent $359 billion on civilian employee salaries and benefits in fiscal year 2023. The administration estimates an annual savings of $28 billion from these layoffs, according to McLaurine Pinover, spokesperson for the Office of Personnel Management.

Published date: October 01 2025, 01:35

Title: 'Intention to dismantle': Federal workers fear 'massacre' as Trump plays 'game of chicken' with gov

Summary: 
President Donald Trump is preparing to use a government shutdown to conduct mass firings of federal employees, according to The Atlantic. This effort is being driven by White House Budget Director Russell Vought, who aims to shrink the federal bureaucracy and implement the goals of Project 2025, a far-right Christian nationalist agenda published by the Heritage Foundation. Although approximately 275,000 federal workers—over 10% of the workforce—have voluntarily left by December 2025, Sen. Richard Blumenthal (D-CT) estimates the downsizing has already cost American taxpayers $21 billion in direct expenses. Beyond financial costs, Blumenthal warns the impact is 'wide-ranging and pervasive' and cannot be measured solely in dollars. The Atlantic reports that the wave of voluntary departures has normalized the idea of drastic civil service reductions. Following Elon Musk’s appointment to lead the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE), the number of civilian federal workers dropped from 2.4 million to 2.1 million. Vought has now instructed federal agencies to prepare for significant 'reduction-in-force' notices (RIFs) to eliminate personnel and projects not aligned with Trump’s priorities. Some federal workers, including a former VA nurse, resigned early with full pay and benefits, fearing a 'massacre' based on their reading of Project 2025. According to Abby André, executive director of the Impact Project, federal workers have become an afterthought in the second Trump administration, and this administration is more willing than past ones to follow through on threats, transforming a shutdown from a temporary paid vacation into a 'life-altering event.'

Published date: September 30 2025, 13:47
